newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel down, jet extends rise.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel down, jet extends rise.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market slipped on Tuesday amid abundant offers at lower levels while a local trader's sustained bids helped to support jet fuel values, traders said.

Traders noted that reduced gas oil values in Asia, partly due to lower purchase prices by two Singapore traders who were seen buying fewer cargoes, were making it less attractive to ship in gas oil from Europe to Asia.

They said the arbitrage window could have even slammed shut as prices in Europe continued to rise, with gas oil futures on London's International Exchange (IPE) broke through mid-month resistance on Tuesday due to agressive buying from two large players.

With June last trading at $167.25 per tonne, up $1.25 from Monday, the East-West spread for June has narrowed to about $15 per tonne, from about $30 at its peak in March, which attracted over two million tonnes from the West.
Traders said the higher prices in Europe were also influenced by strong U.S. heating oil prices.

But they noted that despite the closed arbitrage, prices in Asia were not expected to rebound as regional supplies would be plentiful as Asian refineries return from maintenance turnarounds. Regional demand was not expected to be strong either and a lot would depend on China's imports, they said. India's June imports were also not expected to be large enough to support prices.
After buying 4.0-4.5 million barrels for May, Indonesia was expected to buy the same volume for June, traders said.

Traders said another 300,000 barrels were bought by a Singapore trader--the first cargo from a European major at $26.20 per tonne for May 24-28 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis, and a second cargo at $26.50 for May 14-18 lifting from a Swiss trader.
These deals indicated a 20-cent dip from Monday's trades as eight sellers emerged.
Jet fuel traded firmer with 100,000 barrels sold by a US trader to a European major at $25.25 per barrel for May 14-18 lifting fob, about 75 cents above Monday's deal.
